clue.text: See 3
Mean to add extra material to the reference level

parts.note: mean, as in low or contemptible, gives base
to line a coat is to add an extra layer of material inside it

explanation.surface: A statistician weighs whether padding the data shifts the average used as a benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseline is the starting measurement against which later values are compared.

clue.text: Game of chance and fate as well? Not entirely

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny

indicators.note: not entirely tells us to drop the last letter of the word for 'as well'

parts.note: as well means too, in addition

explanation.surface: A gambler wonders whether a game of luck is ruled partly by destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' clips the last letter off the word for 'as well'; the question mark covers 'fate' doubling as a hint at luck.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bingo-like game where numbers are drawn at random, so winning is pure luck.

clue.text: Locker in which man kept his treasure while away?

definitions.text: Locker in which man kept his treasure while away?

parts.words: Locker in which man kept his treasure while away
parts.note: a 'locker' sounds like a sea chest, but it is a device that locks; the 'treasure' a departing knight guarded was his wife's fidelity

explanation.surface: A sailor stows his valuables in a sea chest before a long voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Medieval legend says crusaders locked their wives into such a garment before leaving, so the 'treasure' is the wife's virtue, not gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says a crusader locked this garment on his wife so her fidelity stayed secure during his absence.

clue.text: Misbehaving children? Number getting grabbed

definitions.meaning: an unruly child is called a real ..., someone hard to manage
a small quantity, as much as a hand can grab at once

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a troublesome person who is hard to control, and the amount one hand can hold.

clue.text: The consequence of trouble brewing?

parts.note: trouble brewing reads as a crisis building, but the brewing is literal, tea made in a small vessel, where any upset is trivial

explanation.surface: Ominous signs suggest a crisis is about to break.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means a fuss over nothing; the clue pictures the tempest literally inside the vessel where tea brews.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a great fuss over a trivial matter, a tempest confined to a tiny vessel.

clue.text: A repeated feature magnetism and energy share

parts.note: 'it' is sex appeal or personal magnetism, as in the 'It girl'
E is the physics symbol for energy
a ration is a fixed share or allowance

explanation.surface: A physics textbook notes a property that magnetism and energy have in common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Share' looks like a verb saying magnetism and energy have something in common, but it is a noun for RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Each repetition of a process is one pass through it, so a recurring feature is that process's repetition.

clue.text: It goes up and down — openings for you often will recur

indicators.note: recur means happen again, so the two letters picked are written twice
openings are beginnings, so we take the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A guide to a toy says the opening moves for you will come round often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openings for' takes Y and O from 'you often'; 'will recur' doubles that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy spool on a string that climbs and drops as the player flicks the wrist.

clue.text: Well-oiled, perhaps, finding non-alcoholic drink distasteful?

parts.note: water is the plainest drink with no alcohol
something repellent is distasteful or repugnant

explanation.surface: A drunk, well-oiled, recoils at being offered a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-oiled' is British slang for drunk, which suits the surface; here it means coated with oil so rain runs off.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface coated with oil sheds rain, so it resists getting wet; 'perhaps' marks oiling as one example.

clue.text: Ache almost entirely linked to gland

parts.note: to pine is to ache with longing

indicators.note: almost signals that the word for 'entirely' loses its final letter

parts.note: entirely means all, wholly

explanation.surface: A pain that is nearly total is traced to a gland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' clips the last letter off the word for 'entirely'; the definition is adjectival, 'linked to gland', as in the pineal gland of the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the small gland deep in the brain that secretes melatonin.

clue.text: 0TV programme — it is documentary broadcast about love? Not right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the letter for love
broadcast means scattered widely, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder

indicators.note: not right asks for R, the abbreviation for right, to be removed from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a documentary aired about romance gets things wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' removes R from IT IS DOCUMENTARY; 'broadcast' shuffles the rest and 'about' wraps those letters around O (love).
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a broadcast comic series built around a fixed set of characters and settings.

clue.text: Describing binder for paper made from deciduous trees?

definitions.text: Describing binder for paper made from deciduous trees?

parts.words: Describing binder for paper made from deciduous trees
parts.note: a ring binder holds removable sheets, while deciduous trees shed, or let go of, their foliage each autumn

explanation.surface: A stationer describes a folder made from the wood of trees that shed every autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'paper' is a sheet in a folder; the question mark points to trees whose leaves come loose and fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring binders hold detachable sheets that can be removed or added freely, like foliage dropping from branches.

clue.text: Some limeade — or something stronger?

indicators.note: some means part of, so the answer is a run of letters inside the word limeade

explanation.surface: Someone at a bar is offered lime soda, or perhaps a harder drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'limeade' sit four letters forming an ancient alcoholic drink, stronger than the soft drink around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey wine is alcoholic, so it is a stronger drink than the soft drink named in the clue.

clue.text: Figure mule ran off

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, part of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A mule bolted off down the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges MULE RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit such as 7 or the Roman XII is a written sign for a number.

clue.text: Soldiers occupying street and prison of Mediterranean island

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so the soldiers go between the words for street and prison

parts.note: a mall is a broad avenue or shopping street, like London's Mall
can is slang for prison
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Troops take over a street and a jail on a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is a crossword staple for soldiers; 'occupying' sets them between the street and the prison words. The Mall is a famous London avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things from the largest Balearic island, off Spain's east coast.

clue.text: Time of fasting not entirely bad-here's a vegetable

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

indicators.note: not entirely asks for the last letter of the word for bad to be dropped

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: During a period of fasting, a vegetable dish is not so bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' clips the final letter off the word for bad; the hyphen in 'bad-here's' is a printing join, and 'here's a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lens-shaped pulse, the seed of a legume, cooked in soups and dals.

clue.text: Severe worry evident in German criminal

indicators.note: evident in means showing inside, so the worry is placed within the abbreviation for German

parts.note: angst is intense anxiety or dread

explanation.surface: A German lawbreaker shows signs of intense anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evident in' acts as a container signal: the worry shows inside the abbreviation for German, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobster is a member of an organised gang of lawbreakers.

clue.text: Mistake that gets students recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for students is read backwards

parts.note: pupils are students at school

explanation.surface: A school blunder means the students are sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reverses PUPILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A small blunder or error, the kind made through carelessness.

clue.text: Prudish joke about woman

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the joke goes around the woman's name

parts.note: a pun is a joke playing on words
Rita is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A strait-laced person makes a crack about a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is a container signal: the word for joke surrounds the woman's name. Any common female name can stand for 'woman' in cryptics.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, it describes someone strict in morals who disapproves of pleasure.

clue.text: Doomed liner not about to be given a Queen's name

indicators.note: not tells us to remove the letter for about from the liner's name

parts.note: the Titanic was the liner that sank on its maiden voyage in 1912
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: An ill-fated ship is renamed after a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not about' removes C (circa) from TITANIC; 'to be given a' then adds A.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream the queen of the fairies is called this.

clue.text: Whip's target beginning to grovel at foot of party leader

indicators.note: at foot of says the letter goes at the end, below the word for party in this down clue

parts.note: a whipping top is a toy spun by lashing it with a whip
a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A party whip makes members grovel before the leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In a political party the whip enforces discipline, but here the 'whip's target' is a spinning top. 'Beginning to' takes G, which 'at foot of' places after DO.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the dominant figure, the boss who has come out on top.

clue.text: Black bird-and where it's baked in pie?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A dark bird recalls the nursery rhyme of blackbirds baked in a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the nursery rhyme of four and twenty blackbirds baked in a pie; here the pie's filling is cooked in a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep round dish holds the filling while the pie cooks in the oven.

clue.text: Salesman getting consumer activity occurring again

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
eating is consuming food, the activity of a consumer

explanation.surface: A salesman notes shoppers' habits coming round again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer activity' suggests shopping, but the consuming is literal: eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that keeps coming round again is recurring, happening over and over.

clue.text: What's seen in limits of intelligence? That is

parts.words: What's seen in limits of intelligence
parts.note: the first and last letters of the word intelligence are I and E, the abbreviation whose full Latin form this is

explanation.walkthrough: The 'limits' of 'intelligence' are its first and last letters, I and E, the familiar abbreviation; the answer is the Latin phrase it stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'that is', introducing a clarification, and is abbreviated i.e.

clue.text: Saying little, being heartless regarding ordinary people

indicators.note: heartless asks for the central letters to be cut out of the word for saying little

parts.note: laconic means terse, using few words

explanation.surface: A taciturn, unfeeling official speaks about the common folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being heartless' removes the middle CON from LACONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: It means relating to the laity, ordinary people as distinct from clergy.

clue.text: Pyramid, for example, minute men cannot shift

indicators.note: shift means move, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, part of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Tiny workers are unable to move a massive pyramid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' rearranges MINUTE MEN CANNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt's pyramids are prime examples of very old structures preserved for their historical value.

clue.text: Unremitting damage after incursion of new insect

indicators.note: incursion means an invasion, so the letter for new breaks into the word for damage

parts.note: cost means damage or loss, as in counting the cost
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Constant damage follows a fresh insect invasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After incursion of' signals that the abbreviation for new breaks into the word for damage; the insect then simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unceasing never lets up, persisting without pause.

clue.text: Famous actor's short debut

indicators.note: short tells us the word for debut loses its last letter

parts.note: a debut is a start, a first appearance

explanation.surface: A famous actor's first appearance was brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts START to STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated performer who heads the cast and draws audiences.
